title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: edit ServiceNow user mapping and query filters on a published connection
summary: The briefing assumes an admin-opt-in default that Microsoft's description of the editing capability does not explicitly establish, and its Copilot Studio licensing statement omits the Microsoft 365 prerequisite. The editing capability and roadmap details are supported, but the query-filter guidance should also disclose Microsoft's conflicting connector FAQ.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk, impact
claims.claim: The change is admin-opt-in and nothing changes in a tenant until an AI administrator edits a connection.
claims.quote: Searched: '503590 default'; 'Microsoft 365 ServiceNow connection edit user mapping query filter default rollout admin opt in'. Read the roadmap, release notes, manage-connector and ServiceNow Knowledge deployment pages; none explicitly states this change's arrival default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown'. Replace 'Nothing changes until an AI administrator edits the connection' in the summary with 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival'. Replace the opening of the second paragraph of Why it matters with 'Microsoft has not stated this change's arrival default; no source says existing connection behaviour changes. Review existing ServiceNow connections against current needs.' In the risk rationale replace 'and nothing changes until an administrator makes one' with 'and no source says existing connection behaviour changes on arrival'. Remove the impact rationale's assertion that end users see a difference only if an edit is made; retain 'Low. This is an administrator-side connection-editing capability.' The documented manual editing procedure does not itself establish a rollout default.
